contexts.text: Let there be no contention between me and thee () = no discord between them. AC 1577:end.
Continual contentions in the things of faith. Signified.

He called the name of the well Ezek, because they contended with him () = denial on account of these things... To quarrel, or contend = to deny... By Ezek, or contention, is signified the denial of the internal sense of the Word. AC 3428.
Because as a prince thou hast contended with God and with men, and thou hast prevailed () = continual victories in combats as to truths and goods. To contend as a prince = to conquer in combats.
To contend with God, in the historical sense, = to be urgent that there might be the representative of a Church with them.
See that ye fall not out in the way () = that they are in tranquillity.
Contention among themselves about truths. Signified.
That the Lord would contend with them from the Word. Signified.
Its contentions with those who will be of the New Church. Signified.
